xg.definition: Expected goals. The probability a shot becomes a goal, given only the information the model is allowed to see.

tracking-data.definition: Positions of the players and the ball sampled many times a second. This is not the same thing as a list of tagged events.

event-data.definition: A log of discrete actions such as passes, carries, and shots, usually with a location. Freeze frames, when present, are a snapshot around one event, not a full tracking feed.

substitute-data.definition: A public dataset used in place of the data the paper actually fit. A page that does this must show the Rebuilt on substitute data callout and say what does not transfer.

epa.definition: Expected points added. The change in expected points from the start of a play to the end of it.

epv.definition: Expected possession value. A number for how a possession is expected to end, updated as the players and the ball move.

big-data-bowl.definition: The NFL's public analytics competition. Some years release player-tracking files that a paper can be rebuilt on directly.

statcast.definition: MLB's tracking of the ball and the players. Baseball Savant publishes a public slice of it, including pitch-level and batted-ball fields.

msne.definition: A Nash equilibrium in which at least one player randomises, chosen so the other player gains nothing by switching.

best-response.definition: The move that does best against a given move by the opponent.

goal-partition.definition: One of the eight cells of the goal face used to bin penalty kicks.

conversion-rate.definition: Goals divided by attempts to a cell.

leave-one-out.definition: A statistic computed without the current row, so that row cannot influence itself.

off-target-share.definition: Misses divided by misses plus saves for a cell: among the kicks that did not score, the share that missed the frame.

lasso.definition: Regression that shrinks coefficients with an L1 penalty λ.

bootstrap.definition: Resampling the data to estimate how much a statistic varies.

indifference-curve.definition: Combinations of two rates the shooter likes equally.
